layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Temperature as a Crevice Corrosion Criterion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: R. J. BRIGHAM*

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Using temperature as a crevice corrosion criterion, a number of commercial and experimental

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo-bearing 18% Cr austenitic stainiess steels have been evaluated for crevice corrosion resistance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These data have been correlated with the effect of Mo content on the rate of active corrosion in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: very aggressive acid solution expected in the crevice itself. Alloyed Mo has been found to play the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dominant role in reducing the relative rate of crevice corrosion and in defining the go/no-go crevice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion behavior in terms of the crevice corrosion temperature (CCT) in oxidizing acid chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions. For 18% Cr austenitic stainless steels the empirical relationship

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has been found.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In earlier presentations,1 ,2 temperature has been shown to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be a reliable pitting criterion for 18% Cr austenitic stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels. For each steel, a temperature, called the critical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting temperature (CPT), has been found below which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pits will not initiate on a flat surface parallel to the rolling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plane when the steel is exposed to oxidizing acid chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions. Molybdenum plays the dominant beneficial role

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in improving pit initiation resistance as measured by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CPT while other alloying additions contribute to a lesser

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extent. Several families of alloys, depending on chemistry,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been identified.2,3 For all of the alloys, edge,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: end-grain, and crevice attack have been observed to occur at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperatures below the CPT. However, further experimen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation has shown that there exists a temperature, which we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: call the crevice corrosion temperature (CCT), below which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: no corrosion of any type will occur even when the alloys

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are tested in a geometric configuration containing a built-in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crevice.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Test Method for Determining CCT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In order to simulate the worst possible crevice configu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ration, three types of crevices have been used: metal to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metal, Teflon to metal, and rubber (elastic band) to metal.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The testing method adopted is an extension of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: technique which proved successful for the quantitative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluation of pit initiation resistance. Samples of stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steel have been exposed to 10% FeCl3 for 24 hours at fixed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperature in at least two of the three crevice configura-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions mentioned above. At the end of one such exposure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: period, the stainless steel was examined visually. If no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion attack of any type could be observed, the sample

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was considered to be immune at that temperature and was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: then exposed for a further 24 hours at a 2.5 C higher

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperature. This procedure was continued until attack of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: any kind (edge, end-grain, elastic to metal crevice, metal to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metal crevice, etc) was observed. The CCT was bracketed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by that 2.5 C temperature interval in which the go/no-go

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: characteristics were observed. Go/no-go results obtained in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 24 hour tests were routinely confirmed in 66 hour tests and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the case of one alloy, the CCT was found to be valid for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a 30 day exposure in 10% FeCl3. All of the alloys were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tested in the single-phase quench-annealed condition with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: abraded surfaces (120 grit silicon carbide)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Because Mo has been found to play the dominant role

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in increasing resistance to crevice corrosion, the results for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: several steels are plotted as CCT vs %Mo as shown in Figure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. The values obtained are compared in Figure 1 with CPT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vs %Mo for four families of 18% Cr austenitic alloys which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been defined previously.2,3 Chemical analyses, CCT,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and pitting family for each of the alloys are given in Table

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Family 1 represents the average family of alloys

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corresponding to present day commercial practice. Family

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 represents a series of alloys similar to Family 1, but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: having a higher nitrogen content. Family 3 represents a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: series of alloys similar to Family 1, but containing low Mn

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (<0.5% Mn). Family 4 represents a series of high Si (3.5%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Si) stainless steels. The CPT vs %Mo characteristics of these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: four families along with the appropriate equation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behavior are plotted in Figure 1.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Whereas several distinct families of alloys can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: observed in the case of pit initiation resistance, all of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys apparently fall in the same family with respect to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crevice corrosion resistance. Their behavior can be de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scribed empirically by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The data are plotted as error bars with the low temperature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Submitted for publication May, 1974.

layout_dets.text: CORROSION-NACE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FIGURE 1 - Crevice corrosion temperature (CCT) and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: critical pitting temperature (CPT) as a function of molyb-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denum content for several austenitic stainless steels. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: numbers associated with the CCT data refer to alloys listed in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Table 1, while the numbers on the CPT data denote the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting families listed in the same table.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: end denoting no attack and the high temperature end

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denoting attack. Within the 10 C scatter-band, no distin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guishing features can be observed for alloys on the upper or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lower limits of the band. Alloyed Mo, however, produces

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the well established trend toward higher resistance to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crevice corrosion with increasing additions shown in Figure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While the CPT parameter describes conditions for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nucleation of pits on a flat surface, the CCT parameter is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: related to the conditions for zero growth rate of a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pre-existing pit or other occluded cell. These quantities

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: therefore are characteristic of the most severe (CCT) and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: least severe (CPT) degrees of occlusion possible. Conse-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quently, most alloys in service conditions in chloride

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions such as sea water would be expected to have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance between these extremes, depending on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: severity the crevice condition encountered. For samples

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with severe artificial crevices exposed 3 years in sea water in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Halifax Harbor (maximum temperature 15 C), go/no-go

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crevice corrosion behavior was observed which is consistent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the data in Figure 1. For example, Alloys 7, 10, 13, 15

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which contain more than 5.6% Mo, showed no crevice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attack, while Alloy 5 and similar alloys containing less than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.5% Mo were attacked during this exposure.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Rate of Crevice Corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The data presented above for CCT vs %Mo, although

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: empirical in nature, have established a limit for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance for 18% Cr austenitic alloys in oxidizing acid

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride media. They also serve as a basis for a better

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: understanding of the crevice corrosion phenomenon when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: considered in combination with other observations. Picker-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing and Frankenthal⁴ observed that hydrogen gas is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: produced in occluded cells in stainless steels. This observa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion unequivocally fixed the potential-pH conditions in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: occluded geometry below the hydrogen line and in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: active corrosion region of the Pourbaix diagram. Suzuki et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: measured the chloride concentration and pH of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution in artificial occluded cells and found values of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: order of 6.5N chloride and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for Mo-bearing stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels corroding galvanostatically in 0.5N NaCl bulk solu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion. If the maximum acidity were approximately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the maximum chloride content approximately 10M for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the most severe conditions, the chemistry of the occluded

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: area could be considered to approach that of concentrated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HCl (37.5% HCl). It is therefore possible to estimate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relative rates of crevice corrosion by studying the active

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion rate of stainless steels in concentrated HCl.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Molybdenum content and temperature, the dominant fac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tors in determining CCT, were chosen as the variables.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The results are plotted as corrosion rate (ipm) vs Mo

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content in Figure 2. Equivalent current densities are also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown, assuming for simplicity that all of the ions go into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution in the 2+ valence state. At low Mo levels, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion rate decreases logarithmically with increasing Mo

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content. At rates less than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ipm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cm/month), weight loss results become inaccurate and seem

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to represent the minimum readily measurable in this type

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of experiment. However, if the curves are extrapolated as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown to a typical passive current density

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the Mo level expected to be required to attain this current

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: density at each temperature can be determined. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: example, at 0, 25, and 50 C approximately 4.5, 6, and 8%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo respectively are expected to be needed for a corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rate characteristic of passivity in these steels. When these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: values are compared with the CCT (%Mo vs temperature)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data of Figure 1, a reasonable correlation is obtained.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Using two independent testing techniques, temperature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has been shown to be a reliable criterion for defining

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: go/no-go conditions for crevice corrosion in wholly austen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: itic stainless steels containing nominally 18% Cr. In these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels, alloyed Mo plays the dominant role in increasing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crevice corrosion resistance while, in contrast to the pit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: initiation parameters, the effects of other alloying additions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been found to be minimal. Alloys with CPT varying

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from Family 1 to Family 4 in Figure 1 have been shown to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have the same CCT characteristics within the ±5 C scatter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: band. Although the theoretical significance of these data is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not clear at present, the CCT values can be used to define

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: empirically the limits of immunity of stainless steels to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: crevice corrosion in an environment such as sea water which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has a chloride activity similar to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: here.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Apart from the effect of alloyed Mo in defining

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: go/no-go crevice corrosion behavior, the results of Figure 2

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: show the effect of Mo on the relative rates of crevice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion attack for 18% Cr austenitic steels at tempera-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures above the CCT. Even when attack is expected, these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data show that a 10-fold decrease in corrosion rate can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: expected with a 1.5% increase in alloyed Mo. Although the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: absolute values of CCT may be such that choosing a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: completely resistance steel is impractical, important de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creases in corrosion rate can be expected with higher Mo

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels.
